The expected length is at most $n$, so $\alpha \le 0$. For chronological loop erasure in $\mathbb{Z}^4$, the loop-erasure of an $n$-step walk has expected length of order $n(\log n)^{-1/3}$, and I recall that the largest-loop-first version in dimension four has the same exponent. I did not verify this by derivation or by checking the literature, so treat it as a recollection rather than a proof.
